papers.title: Effect of Post-Weld Heat Treatment on Residual Stress and Fatigue Crack Propagation Behavior in Linear Friction Welded Ti-6Al-4V Alloy
papers.abstract: In this study, the effects of post-weld heat treatment (PWHT) on residual stress distribution and fatigue crack propagation (FCP) behavior in linear friction welded (LFW) Ti-6Al-4V joints were investigated. Microstructural evolution in the weld center zone (WCZ), thermomechanically affected zone (TMAZ), heat-affected zone (HAZ), and base metal (BM) was characterized using scanning electron microscropy (SEM) and electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD). Mechanical properties were evaluated via Vickers hardness testing and digital image correlation (DIC)-based tensile testing. Residual stresses before and after PWHT were measured using the contour method. The LFW process introduced significant residual stresses, with tensile stresses up to 709.2 MPa in the WCZ, resulting in non-uniform fatigue crack growth behavior. PWHT at 650 °C and 750 °C effectively reduced these stresses. After PWHT, fatigue cracks propagated uniformly across the weld region, enabling reliable determination of crack growth rates. The average crack growth rates of the heat-treated specimens were comparable to those of the base metal, confirming that PWHT, particularly at 750 °C, stabilizes the fatigue crack path and relieves internal stress.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及线性摩擦焊而非增材制造，因此与方向不直接相关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper studies welded joints, not additive manufactured components; therefore, it does not address post-processing of AM Ti-6Al-4V.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究PWHT对线性摩擦焊Ti-6Al-4V接头残余应力和疲劳裂纹扩展的影响。
summary_zh.method: 采用SEM、EBSD、硬度测试、DIC拉伸和轮廓法测量残余应力。
summary_zh.result: PWHT有效降低了残余应力，使疲劳裂纹均匀扩展，速率与母材相当。
summary_zh.validation: 通过轮廓法测量残余应力，并与疲劳试验结果对比验证。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate how post-weld heat treatment affects residual stress and fatigue crack propagation in linear friction welded Ti-6Al-4V joints.
summary_en.method: Microstructural characterization (SEM, EBSD), mechanical testing (hardness, DIC tensile), and residual stress measurement (contour method) were conducted.
summary_en.result: Post-weld heat treatment at 650°C and 750°C significantly reduced residual stresses, leading to uniform fatigue crack growth with rates similar to base metal.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation through residual stress contour method and fatigue crack growth rate comparison.

papers.title: Hydroxyapatite/Graphene Composite Anticorrosion Coating on Ti-6Al-4V: Fabrications and Trend
papers.abstract: Orthopedics implants have become more crucial for bone replacement as the need for bone replacement increases. Titanium alloy Ti-6Al-4V is widely used as an orthopedic implant due to its high biocompatibility and superior mechanical properties. However, it has several serious drawbacks, such as low corrosion resistance. In order to overcome this demerit, coatings should be applied. Hydroxyapatite, a mineral similar to bone composition, is a good candidate for this purpose. By compositing hydroxyapatite with graphene, the mechanical properties and adhesion of the coating are enhanced. Various coating methods are employed to fabricate this composite coating. This work summarizes and discusses trends, fabrication techniques, and the future perspectives of hydroxyapatite/graphene as a Ti-6Al-4V implant coating.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文讨论Ti-6Al-4V的涂层，而非股骨柄的结构设计或力学性能。
llm.why_not_core: Paper does not address femoral stem structural design, lattice architecture, stress shielding, fatigue testing, or any mechanical/biomechanical analysis of stems; it is a review on anticorrosion coatings.

summary_en.motivation: To improve the corrosion resistance of Ti-6Al-4V orthopedic implants through coatings.
summary_en.method: This work reviews trends, fabrication techniques, and future perspectives of hydroxyapatite/graphene composite coatings on Ti-6Al-4V.
summary_en.result: A summary of current trends and future directions for hydroxyapatite/graphene coatings is provided.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; the paper is a literature review.
